items.title: FAA ground stop lifted but nationwide airline recovery extends into Saturday
items.summary: The FAA lifted Friday's nationwide departure ground stop around 8:15 p.m. ET after communications failures, but airlines face extensive Saturday cancellations as crews and aircraft are repositioned. Early Saturday reports count thousands of canceled flights. This is a verified operational disruption, not a confirmed Saturday equity-price move.

observations.label: Ground stop lifted
observations.value: November 13 approximately 8:15 p.m. EST, FAA statement reported by CBS and AP

observations.label: Saturday cancellation reports
observations.value: Over 2,500 cancellations reported by AP; Washington Post cited over 3,200 at its reporting observation; counts evolve

observations.label: Risks and next indicators
observations.value: Weekend cancellations, crew and aircraft repositioning, airline guidance, FAA communications stability and Monday share reaction; rapid recovery would limit impact

items.key_finding: A resolved nationwide ground stop has become a multiday airline network-recovery risk.

sources.title: CBS News FAA ground stop lifted

items.title: Friday close confirms broad AI semiconductor and networking weakness
items.summary: Friday's regular-session close confirmed AMD down about 8.8%, Broadcom down 4.8% and Nvidia down 2.0%, while the Nasdaq fell 0.9%. Cisco and Coherent also declined sharply, indicating wider AI infrastructure risk repricing. The decline is evidence of sector pressure, not proof of collapsing end demand.

observations.label: November 13 regular-session closes
observations.value: AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, NVDA -2.0%; Nasdaq -0.9% (rounded)

observations.label: Adjacent infrastructure declines
observations.value: Cisco -6.2%, Coherent -6.0% on Friday

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Semiconductor breadth, hyperscaler capex, Treasury yields, AI credit conditions and Monday recovery; sustained broad rebound would weaken risk-off signal

items.key_finding: Closing prices corroborate a sector-wide chip and networking selloff beyond Nvidia.

items.title: UKMTO weekly assessment maintains severe Hormuz threat despite recovering crude flows
items.summary: UKMTO's November 13 weekly overview rates the Strait of Hormuz threat severe and the Arabian Gulf substantial. It records 163 events year to date and 141 vessel-damage reports, with the latest listed attacks dated November 11. These figures document sustained vessel-security risk but do not establish a new export shutdown.

observations.label: UKMTO week ending November 13
observations.value: 163 events YTD, 141 vessel-damage reports YTD, 86 injuries/fatalities YTD; reporting range through November 11

observations.label: JMIC regional risk
observations.value: Strait of Hormuz SEVERE, Arabian Gulf SUBSTANTIAL, Gulf of Oman MODERATE

observations.label: New verified oil flow loss
observations.value: None established in this research pass

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO/MARAD incidents, vessel transits, Gulf exports, tanker insurance/freight, diesel cracks, Brent/WTI and XLE/XOP; sustained safe transit would ease security risk

items.key_finding: Severe documented shipping danger persists without fresh verified physical crude export loss.

items.title: Fermi jumps as FT identifies Amazon behind proposed 600 MW hyperscaler project
items.summary: Fermi rallied sharply Friday after the Financial Times identified Amazon as the customer behind its announced 600 MW Project Matador development agreements. Fermi confirmed upfront funding arrangements but has not identified the customer or signed a definitive long-term lease. The company remains pre-revenue and highly exposed to financing and construction execution risks.

observations.label: Market reaction, Nov 13 at 3:46 PM EST
observations.value: Yahoo Finance reported FRMI $2.575, up 25.0%, intraday; not an official close

observations.label: Reported Nov 13 4 PM price, one quote provider
observations.value: StockAnalysis listed FRMI $2.61, up 26.70%; second independent closing-price confirmation not obtained, so not graded confirmed

observations.label: Confirmed customer agreements announced Nov 12
observations.value: 600 MW initial development beginning in 2027; $200 million prepayment arrangement and $15 million early-construction agreement; contemplated $90 million materials agreement

observations.label: Customer identification qualification
observations.value: FT identified Amazon on Nov 13 citing unnamed sources; company has not publicly identified the customer or executed a definitive long-term lease

observations.label: Company financial position
observations.value: Fermi Q3 net loss $141.6 million, September 30 net debt roughly $958.4 million, pre-revenue; earlier TensorWave lease and AMD credit support terminated

observations.label: Risk and invalidation indicators
observations.value: Watch confirmation from Amazon, actual funding receipt, definitive lease/financing, December 1 construction mobilization, December 31 tenant milestone and 2027 power delivery; failed milestones reverse the recovery narrative

items.key_finding: A potential marquee customer is validating power-ready sites, but funding and binding leases lag the market repricing.

items.title: Coast Guard closes three-mile Mississippi River section after New Orleans tanker collision
items.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard halted vessel traffic between Mississippi River mile markers 93 and 96 after the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck a docked river cruise ship in New Orleans. This is a verified disruption to a major shipping corridor, but no petroleum export losses, refinery outage or commodity-price impact has been established. Reopening and vessel queues determine commercial significance.

observations.label: Incident November 13
observations.value: Approximately 12:30 PM Central (1:30 PM EST); tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with docked American Heritage river cruise vessel in New Orleans.

observations.label: Verified physical-flow restriction
observations.value: Coast Guard reported Mississippi River closed to vessel traffic at mile marker 96; reporting identifies restricted area between river miles 93 and 96.

observations.label: Market impact assessment
observations.value: No verified crude or petroleum-product export curtailment, refinery shutdown, cargo loss or price move attributable to the collision at research cutoff.

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Coast Guard reopening and safety notices; downstream and upstream vessel queues; petrochemical and oil-product barge delays. Rapid reopening with no cargo delays would limit market effect.

items.key_finding: A confirmed three-mile Mississippi River closure creates a physical maritime bottleneck, with energy-market consequences unquantified.
